title: Tableau Failed Logins and Access Audit
dataSources: Tableau Server logs (`tableau:backgrounder`, `tableau:vizqlserver`, `tableau:httpd`), `workgroup` repository tables (`background_jobs`, `http_requests`, `_views_stats`, `licensing`) via DB Connect, Tableau Cloud Admin Insights / Activity Log exports.
app: Splunk DB Connect (Splunkbase 2686) against the Tableau Server `workgroup` PostgreSQL repository; Tableau Server logs via Universal Forwarder; Tableau Server REST API and TSM metrics via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=bi sourcetype=tableau:vizportal (action=login OR action=logout OR action=access_denied)
| stats count as attempts, sum(eval(result="failure")) as failures by user, action
| where failures>5
| sort - failures
description: Summarises Tableau sign-in activity and surfaces users with repeated failed logins or access-denied events, supporting both troubleshooting and abuse detection.
value: Repeated failed logins can mean a locked-out executive before a board meeting or a credential-stuffing attempt; auditing access keeps the platform both usable and secure.
implementation: Ingest vizportal/application logs; schedule hourly; alert on bursts of failures per user or source. Route security-relevant patterns to your SOC.
visualization: Table of users by failures, timechart of failed logins, alert.
grandmaExplanation: We keep a record of who signs in to your reporting tool and flag lots of failed attempts, which could be someone locked out or someone who should not be trying.
